# Repository guidance

## Conventions

Keep reusable behavior in src/index.ts and process I/O in src/cli.ts. Use strict TypeScript, node:test and node:assert/strict. CLI tests spawn the real process. README owns runnable commands; roadmap/roadmap.config.json owns gate bindings. Keep requirements, architecture and UX in their independent linked homes.

## Don't

Do not introduce framework runtime, external services, authentication, mobile UI, product remotes, publishing or deployment. Do not invent tokens, duplicate conventions into harness files, assume plugin-internal paths in consumer code, or commit in this fixture.

## Generalize-forward

Extract shared abstractions when a second real consumer needs them. Preserve the small API/process boundary until then.

## Flag-first delivery

Future user-facing changes require a flag lifecycle or an approved reason that a flag is inapplicable. Keep new flags disabled until rollout approval. Keep release-only work in hold[]; this fixture authorizes no release or deployment.

## Planning

Use the installed zeroh-roadmap phase workflow for subsequent development. Preserve existing homes and generated harness blocks byte-identically unless an exact repair is separately approved.
@AGENTS.md

AGENTS.md is the sole conventions home. Keep only harness-specific guidance here.
# Contributing

Follow [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) and the verification commands in [README](README.md). Add behavior tests when public behavior changes. Keep docs concise, current and linked to one authoritative home per fact.

Use concise imperative commit subjects in ordinary repositories. Commits are forbidden in this native fixture.
# greenfield-proof

A private TypeScript greeting API and CLI for developers. See [PRD](docs/PRD.md) and [UX canon](docs/ux-canon.md).

## Structure

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| src/index.ts | Reusable greeting API |
| src/cli.ts | Executable process adapter |
| test/ | API and real CLI subprocess tests |
| tsup.config.ts | ESM build and declarations |
| dist/ | Built API and CLI |
| docs/ | Product, ADR, standards, architecture and UX homes |
| roadmap/ | Copied schema, registry, emitter, config, phases and arcs |
| reviews/ | Emitted changelog and release-review home |
| scripts/ | Copied catalog, delivery and review tooling |
| .github/greenfield-delivery.json | Delivery execution contract |
| .github/workflows/ci.yml | Affected/local/full lifecycle and authoritative backstop |
| .github/workflows/release.yml | Exact-artifact verification; promotion unavailable |

## Commands

Use Node 22.12+ on Linux. Set npm_config_cache=$PWD/.npm-cache and npm_config_logs_dir=$PWD/.npm-logs for npm commands so caches stay local.

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| npm ci --no-audit --no-fund | Install the retained lockfile |
| npm run typecheck | Check source, build config and roadmap types |
| npm test | Full local API and CLI behavior suite |
| npm run build | Build dist with tsup |
| node dist/cli.js --help | Built CLI smoke |
| npm run emit:phases | Emit reviews/changelog.json |
| npm run changelog:md | Optional later Markdown changelog generation |
| node scripts/ci-shard-plan.mjs affected | PR checks using real BASE_SHA; intentionally full tests |

The catalog checker is scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs, bound to project-root mode, source dot and project name greenfield-proof. Lint and browser e2e are explicitly absent. Init's pre-review helper needs real Git history and contains framework-specific checks; it is not this package's verification gate. The dashboard helper and optional Markdown renderer are installed but not executed during setup.

## Delivery

.github/workflows/ci.yml runs the full small suite for PRs because no dependency-aware selector exists. Main/manual full runs inventory real tracked test files, execute exact-once shards, merge actual JUnit and LCOV, build once and produce authoritative evidence. Nightly runs diagnose without authoritative release evidence. The backstop is .github/workflows/ci.yml (authoritative full suite on main/manual runs).

Push planning binds the previous-main SHA; manual full requires approved base_sha. Initial setup assumes the supplied first root/new-main push and explicitly approves the initial baseline in .github/greenfield-delivery.json. The native fixture has no commits; setup does not create history or run hosted CI.

.github/workflows/release.yml verifies the exact previously built artifact. The protected environment is greenfield-validation. Deployment provider none is explicitly unavailable; publishing and deployment are unauthorized. Baseline: 10 tests, 2 units, 80 percent line coverage; two requested shards. Retention: evidence seven days, raw diagnostics three days, verified promotion one day. Workflows preserve canonical immutable pins and least-privilege jobs.

Installed workflow simulations are validation evidence, not a live GitHub run. Approved execution stops before a separate read-only brownfield audit; idempotence is not claimed before that rerun.

## Catalog

<!-- repo-catalog:start -->
| Project | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| greenfield-proof | . | Reusable greeting API and CLI |
<!-- repo-catalog:end -->
# Product requirements

## Product

greenfield-proof is a small TypeScript reusable greeting API plus CLI for developers. [UX canon](ux-canon.md) specifies its behavior.

## Audience

Developers importing a typed greeting function and invoking its CLI.

## Platforms

Node 22+ on Linux; use Node 22.12 or later on that runtime line for the selected generator.

## Constraints

Use npm, TypeScript, tsup and node:test. Private UNLICENSED fixture, no publishing or fixture commits. Adapt cached create-vite 8.3.0 vanilla-ts directly in this scratch repository. Preserve any present home byte-identically; stop if unexpected homes appear.

## Non-goals

No framework runtime, external service, HTTP backend, authentication, mobile, deployment, product remote or publishing. The reusable API is an imported function, not a network service.

## Success signals

Pass meaningful API and CLI tests, typecheck, build, built CLI smoke, the selected catalog comparison, roadmap config check, actual emission and the complete installed delivery suite. Simulations do not prove a hosted CI run or deployment. Execution ends before a separate read-only brownfield re-audit.

## Brand

Non-Blade; no graphical UI. Registry absent/none because there are no UI components. Do not invent tokens, fonts or palette.

## Decisions

| Date | Ruling | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-09-05 | Separate exact APPROVE GREENFIELD PLAN input authorizes the preceding complete plan | This document is created only after that input; the candidate was not approval. |
| 2026-09-05 | [Technology stack](adr/0001-tech-stack.md) | Explicit user selection of the library-cli archetype and minimal test dependencies. |
| 2026-09-05 | [Non-UI design](adr/0002-design-system.md) | Imported API and terminal CLI only. |
| 2026-09-05 | GitHub Actions; protected release environment greenfield-validation; deployment provider none | Supplied choices; deployment is unavailable and unauthorized. |
| 2026-09-05 | Bootstrap the delivery baseline at 10 tests, 2 units and 80 percent line coverage | Initial delivery baseline presented for approval with fixture setup; owner fixture-owner. The exact baselineApproval is in .github/greenfield-delivery.json. |

## Unknowns

Distribution, graphical surfaces, HTTP services, credentials and release date remain unselected. The initial fixture has no commits and an unborn master branch. Delivery assumes the supplied future first root/new-main push with no previous baseline; this setup does not create history or run CI. Live GitHub evidence is unavailable. Revisit through an approved scope change.
# ADR 0001: Technology stack

## Status and date

Accepted after separate greenfield plan approval; 2026-09-05.

## Context

See [PRD](../PRD.md). The API is an imported function, so the backend, web, mobile and monorepo matrices do not apply.

## Options: Library/CLI

Source: installed zeroh-greenfield skills/stack-decision/references/matrices.md. Exact applicable rows:

| option | pros | cons | better when | component reuse | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tsup + node:test | Compact bundling with built-in tests | Two separate tools | Small TypeScript package values minimal test dependencies | Exported modules and fixtures | tsup |
| tsdown + vitest | Modern bundling and rich tests | Additional test dependency | Vite-aligned libraries need fast test ergonomics | Exported modules and test helpers | tsdown |
| unbuild | Convention-led library output | Less explicit build control | Multi-format package follows unjs conventions | Package presets and modules | unbuild |

## Ruling

2026-09-05: tsup + node:test, explicitly selected for this small TypeScript greeting API and CLI with minimal test dependencies. Use npm and Node 22+ Linux. Adapt the library-cli manifest's my-lib destination to this scratch root using the approved cached create-vite entry. Remove the browser demo and Vite dependency.

## Consequences

Keep reusable logic in src/index.ts and process I/O in src/cli.ts. tsup and node:test are separate tools. tsx loads TypeScript tests and copied roadmap tooling with transform caching disabled. Pin direct versions and retain the npm lock. No framework runtime; private UNLICENSED fixture.

## Revisit when

A second package requires workspace coordination, a supported runtime cannot consume ESM, or an approved requirement adds a web, mobile or HTTP surface. Distribution and service requirements remain unknown.
# ADR 0002: Design system

## Status and date

Accepted after separate greenfield plan approval; 2026-09-05.

## Context and options

The user selected a non-Blade imported API and terminal CLI. The installed design-system reference's web/mobile choices do not apply. The supplied applicable choice is no UI design system, registry absent/none. See [PRD](../PRD.md).

## Ruling

2026-09-05: no UI design system; registry absent/none because there are no graphical components. Do not invent fonts, palette, spacing or tokens. [UX canon](../ux-canon.md) owns terminal behavior. No Blade handoff is needed.

## Consequences

No component framework or design runtime. Plain text, stdout/stderr and exit codes define interaction. Future visual branding remains unknown.

## Revisit when

An approved requirement adds the first graphical surface or Blade branding.
# Code style

## Lint

None: no lint configuration or runner is selected. This is an approved absence, not a passing result.

## Format

None: no formatter is configured. Follow nearby TypeScript formatting and the sole conventions home, [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md).

## Types and tests

[tsconfig.json](../tsconfig.json) enables strict checking. Tests use node:test and node:assert/strict, with real CLI subprocesses. [README](../README.md) owns runnable commands.
# Architecture

## Topic index

| Topic | Home |
| --- | --- |
| Requirements and unknowns | [PRD](PRD.md) |
| Package boundary | [Technology ADR](adr/0001-tech-stack.md) |
| Non-UI ruling | [Design ADR](adr/0002-design-system.md) |
| API and terminal behavior | [UX canon](ux-canon.md) |
| Reusable logic | [src/index.ts](../src/index.ts) |
| Process adapter | [src/cli.ts](../src/cli.ts) |
| Build boundary | [tsup.config.ts](../tsup.config.ts) |
| Delivery execution | [Delivery config](../.github/greenfield-delivery.json) |
| Gates and pointers | [Roadmap config](../roadmap/roadmap.config.json) |

## Extend protocol

Keep reusable logic independent of process I/O. Extend the public contract and behavior tests together. Record approved boundary changes in the owning ADR before introducing another package or service. Consumer tooling resolves local homes without assuming plugin-internal paths.
# UX canon

## Visual language

Plain terminal text. Fonts, palette, spacing and visual tokens are inapplicable.

## Component vocabulary

An imported greet(name?: string) function and greenfield-proof CLI. No graphical components or registry.

## Interaction rules

greet() and greet(undefined) return Hello, world!. A supplied nonblank string returns Hello, <name>! with its characters preserved. Empty or whitespace-only names throw TypeError; nonstring JavaScript inputs also throw TypeError.

The CLI accepts zero or one name, prints the greeting plus a newline to stdout and exits 0. The sole --help argument prints usage to stdout and exits 0. Unknown options, extra arguments and blank names print an error and usage to stderr, print no greeting, and exit 1.

    Usage: greenfield-proof [name]
           greenfield-proof --help

## Binding design system

None, per [ADR 0002](adr/0002-design-system.md). Non-Blade; registry absent/none because there is no UI. A new approved requirement is necessary before introducing visual tokens.

# Repository guidance

## Conventions

Keep reusable behavior in src/index.ts and process I/O in src/cli.ts. Use strict TypeScript, node:test and node:assert/strict. CLI tests spawn the real process. README owns runnable commands; roadmap/roadmap.config.json owns gate bindings. Keep requirements, architecture and UX in their independent linked homes.

## Don't

Do not introduce framework runtime, external services, authentication, mobile UI, product remotes, publishing or deployment. Do not invent tokens, duplicate conventions into harness files, assume plugin-internal paths in consumer code, or commit in this fixture.

## Generalize-forward

Extract shared abstractions when a second real consumer needs them. Preserve the small API/process boundary until then.

## Flag-first delivery

Future user-facing changes require a flag lifecycle or an approved reason that a flag is inapplicable. Keep new flags disabled until rollout approval. Keep release-only work in hold[]; this fixture authorizes no release or deployment.

## Planning

Use the installed zeroh-roadmap phase workflow for subsequent development. Preserve existing homes and generated harness blocks byte-identically unless an exact repair is separately approved.
@AGENTS.md

AGENTS.md is the sole conventions home. Keep only harness-specific guidance here.
# Contributing

Follow [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) and the verification commands in [README](README.md). Add behavior tests when public behavior changes. Keep docs concise, current and linked to one authoritative home per fact.

Use concise imperative commit subjects in ordinary repositories. Commits are forbidden in this native fixture.

Developers importing a typed greeting function and invoking its CLI.

No framework runtime, external service, HTTP backend, authentication, mobile, deployment, product remote or publishing. The reusable API is an imported function, not a network service.

Pass meaningful API and CLI tests, typecheck, build, built CLI smoke, the selected catalog comparison, roadmap config check, actual emission and the complete installed delivery suite. An imported greet(name?: string) function and greenfield-proof CLI. No graphical components or registry.

## Component vocabulary

An imported greet(name?: string) function and greenfield-proof CLI. No graphical components or registry.

## Interaction rules

greet() and greet(undefined) return Hello, world!. A supplied nonblank string returns Hello, <name>! with its characters preserved. Empty or whitespace-only names throw TypeError; nonstring JavaScript inputs also throw TypeError.

The user selected a non-Blade imported API and terminal CLI. The installed design-system reference's web/mobile choices do not apply. The supplied applicable choice is no UI design system, registry absent/none. See [PRD](../PRD.md).

## Ruling

2026-09-05: no UI design system; registry absent/none because there are no graphical components. Do not invent fonts, palette, spacing or tokens. [UX canon](../ux-canon.md) owns terminal behavior. No Blade handoff is needed.

## Consequences

No component framework or design runtime. Plain text, stdout/stderr and exit codes define interaction. Future visual branding remains unknown.

## Revisit when

An approved requirement adds the first graphical surface or Blade branding.

## Lint

None: no lint configuration or runner is selected. This is an approved absence, not a passing result.

## Format

None: no formatter is configured. Follow nearby TypeScript formatting and the sole conventions home, [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md).

[tsconfig.json](../tsconfig.json) enables strict checking. Tests use node:test and node:assert/strict, with real CLI subprocesses. [README](../README.md) owns runnable commands.

Keep reusable logic independent of process I/O. Extend the public contract and behavior tests together. Record approved boundary changes in the owning ADR before introducing another package or service. Consumer tooling resolves local homes without assuming plugin-internal paths.

## Visual language

Plain terminal text. Fonts, palette, spacing and visual tokens are inapplicable.

An imported greet(name?: string) function and greenfield-proof CLI. No graphical components or registry.

greet() and greet(undefined) return Hello, world!. A supplied nonblank string returns Hello, <name>! with its characters preserved. Empty or whitespace-only names throw TypeError; nonstring JavaScript inputs also throw TypeError.

The CLI accepts zero or one name, prints the greeting plus a newline to stdout and exits 0. The sole --help argument prints usage to stdout and exits 0. Unknown options, extra arguments and blank names print an error and usage to stderr, print no greeting, and exit 1.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Pre-review automated checks — catches mechanical issues before agent review.
# Run: bash scripts/pre-review.sh <first-commit-sha>
#
# Eliminates 40-50% of typical agent findings (missing tests, banned patterns,
# duplicate utilities, orphaned @contract tags) at near-zero cost.

set -euo pipefail

BASE="${1:-HEAD~1}"
RED='\033[0;31m'
YELLOW='\033[0;33m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
NC='\033[0m'

ERRORS=0
WARNINGS=0

fail() { echo -e "${RED}FAIL:${NC} $1"; ERRORS=$((ERRORS+1)); }
warn() { echo -e "${YELLOW}WARN:${NC} $1"; WARNINGS=$((WARNINGS+1)); }
pass() { echo -e "${GREEN}  OK:${NC} $1"; }

echo "=== Pre-Review Checks (diff from $BASE) ==="
echo

# ── 1. New lib/services/ files must have test files ───────────────────────────
echo "--- New service files need tests ---"
for f in $(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=A "$BASE"..HEAD -- 'lib/services/*.ts' 'lib/business-rules/*.ts' | grep -v __tests__); do
  basename=$(basename "$f" .ts)
  dir=$(dirname "$f")
  test_file="$dir/__tests__/$basename.test.ts"
  if [ -f "$test_file" ]; then
    pass "$f → $test_file exists"
  else
    fail "$f has no test file at $test_file"
  fi
done

# ── 2. No fs.readFileSync in API routes ───────────────────────────────────────
echo "--- No fs.readFileSync in API routes ---"
if grep -rn "fs\.readFileSync\|fs\.readFile\b" app/api/ --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx" 2>/dev/null; then
  fail "fs.readFileSync in API route — use import for JSON (standalone build won't bundle runtime reads)"
else
  pass "No fs.readFileSync in API routes"
fi

# ── 3. No toBeCloseTo on exact arithmetic ─────────────────────────────────────
echo "--- Check toBeCloseTo usage ---"
matches=$(grep -rn "toBeCloseTo" lib/**/__tests__/*.ts 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -n "$matches" ]; then
  warn "toBeCloseTo found — verify these aren't masking rounding bugs on exact values:"
  echo "$matches" | head -5
else
  pass "No toBeCloseTo in service tests"
fi

# ── 4. @contract tags have @spec tests ────────────────────────────────────────
echo "--- @contract tags have @spec coverage ---"
if [ -f "compliance/scripts/check-contract-specs.ts" ]; then
  if npx tsx compliance/scripts/check-contract-specs.ts 2>/dev/null; then
    pass "@contract/@spec alignment verified"
  else
    fail "Orphaned @contract tags without @spec tests"
  fi
else
  pass "@contract spec check script not found (skipped)"
fi

# ── 5. New @contract tags in diff ─────────────────────────────────────────────
echo "--- New @contract tags ---"
new_tags=$(git diff "$BASE"..HEAD -- 'lib/' | grep "^+" | grep "@contract" | grep -v "^+++" || true)
if [ -n "$new_tags" ]; then
  warn "New @contract tags added — verify relationship and confidence:"
  echo "$new_tags" | head -10
fi

# ── 6. No duplicate utility functions ─────────────────────────────────────────
echo "--- Check for duplicate utilities ---"
for f in $(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=AM "$BASE"..HEAD -- '*.ts' '*.tsx' | grep -v __tests__ | grep -v node_modules); do
  # Extract new function names
  new_fns=$(git diff "$BASE"..HEAD -- "$f" | grep "^+.*function " | sed 's/.*function \([a-zA-Z_]*\).*/\1/' | grep -v "^$" || true)
  for fn in $new_fns; do
    # Check if function name exists elsewhere in lib/utils/ or lib/services/
    existing=$(grep -rn "function $fn\b" lib/utils/ lib/services/ --include="*.ts" 2>/dev/null | grep -v "$f" | head -1 || true)
    if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
      warn "Function '$fn' in $f may duplicate: $existing"
    fi
  done
done

# ── 7. DB queries outside try/catch in API routes ─────────────────────────────
echo "--- DB queries in API routes ---"
for f in $(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=AM "$BASE"..HEAD -- 'app/api/**/route.ts'); do
  if grep -q "await db\." "$f" 2>/dev/null; then
    # Check if there's a try/catch wrapping it
    if ! grep -q "try {" "$f" 2>/dev/null; then
      fail "$f has DB queries without try/catch"
    else
      pass "$f has DB queries with try/catch"
    fi
  fi
done

# ── Summary ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo
echo "=== Summary ==="
echo -e "Errors: ${RED}${ERRORS}${NC}  Warnings: ${YELLOW}${WARNINGS}${NC}"
if [ "$ERRORS" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo -e "${RED}Fix errors before running agent review.${NC}"
  exit 1
else
  echo -e "${GREEN}Pre-review checks passed.${NC}"
  exit 0
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# build-dashboard.sh — Rebuild reviews/dashboard/index.html
# Embeds all v*.json review files from reviews/releases/ as inline data.
# Run after adding a new review JSON: bash scripts/build-dashboard.sh
# Output: reviews/dashboard/index.html (self-contained, no CDN except Chart.js)
#
# Resolves reviews/ from the PROJECT ROOT (git toplevel, cwd fallback), never
# from the script's own install dir — scaffold-roadmap.sh installs this file
# to scripts/, where $SCRIPT_DIR-relative paths would read an empty
# scripts/releases/ and silently build an empty dashboard.

set -euo pipefail

PROJECT_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)"
REVIEWS_DIR="$PROJECT_ROOT/reviews"
RELEASES_DIR="$REVIEWS_DIR/releases"
OUTPUT="$REVIEWS_DIR/dashboard/index.html"

[ -d "$RELEASES_DIR" ] || { echo "build-dashboard: no such dir: $RELEASES_DIR (run from the project or a subdir of it)" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p "$REVIEWS_DIR/dashboard"

# Collect all v*.json files into a JSON array using Python
REVIEWS_JSON=$(python3 - "$RELEASES_DIR" <<'PYEOF'
import sys, json, os, glob

releases_dir = sys.argv[1]
files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(releases_dir, 'v*-review.json')))
data = []
for f in files:
    with open(f) as fh:
        data.append(json.load(fh))
print(json.dumps(data, separators=(',', ':')))
PYEOF
)

FILE_COUNT=$(echo "$REVIEWS_JSON" | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(len(json.load(sys.stdin)))')

# Write the HTML using Python to avoid shell escaping issues with JS template literals
python3 - "$OUTPUT" "$REVIEWS_JSON" <<'PYEOF'
import sys, json

output_path = sys.argv[1]

# CI and exact-artifact release

Use the consumer-owned `scripts/ci-shard-plan.mjs` as the sole lifecycle engine.
Copy its two workflows to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `release.yml` only after
approval. Configure `.github/greenfield-delivery.json`; missing configuration,
runner, report parser, baseline, credential or provider is unavailable and exits
nonzero with an install/configuration remedy. A template is not a successful run.

## Approval and configuration

Present the selected adapter, exact inventory/test/build argv, setup commands,
report paths, coverage roots, shard count, count/coverage baselines, affected PR
command, main branch, retention, protected environment and provider placeholders.
Pin dependency versions in the consumer lockfile. Preserve existing workflows;
collisions require an explicit reviewed merge. Never invent credentials or a
working deployment. Provider defaults to unavailable; no arbitrary promotion hook
is accepted. The optional selected provider is `aws-s3-v1`, configured with
`environment`, `bucket`, `region`, `keyPrefix` and an approved OIDC `roleArn`.
The bucket must support versioning and SHA-256 checksums. Other providers require
a separately implemented and verified adapter before use.

Configuration version 1 has `archetype`, `setupArgv` (array of exact argv arrays),
`affectedArgv` (an argv array with a standalone `{base}` token), `shardCount`,
`evidenceDays` (1 through 7), `baseline: {minTests,minUnits,coverageFloor}`,
`adapterConfig: {maxInfraRetries,coverageRoots,leafTasks}`, `runners`, `build`
and `release`. `operationalRoots` explicitly lists dependency/cache/report roots
(defaults `.ci` and `node_modules`); it is also bound in the plan. Each runner binds `inventoryArgv`, `inventoryFormat`, optional
`filePattern`/`pathPrefix`/`targetSuffix`, `shardArgv`, optional reporter `env`,
and `rawReports: [{path,format,from?}]`. Vitest/Playwright also require
`selectionArgv` and `selectionFormat`: the actual pre-run selected file inventory
must equal the single requested unit, or execution stops. `from: stdout` retains the actual process
output as a raw report. Substitutions are whole argv data, never shell evaluation:
`{unit}`, `{reportDir}`, `{junit}`, `{coverage}`. Build binds `argv` and explicit
`outputs` roots; symlinks and overlapping output roots are rejected. The planner
binds the complete runner/build execution contract into `adapterConfigDigest`.
Changing a runner, reporter, output or build command after planning fails.
Production preparation and run/build boundaries verify the exact Git SHA/tree and
an unchanged source snapshot, including ignored/untracked files. Setup/tests may
change only the declared operational roots; build may additionally change its
declared output roots. Other tracked or untracked changes fail.

## Six adapters

Atomic identity is exactly `{runner,canonicalPathOrLeafTask}`. Keep distinct runner
populations disjoint even if two runners reference the same filename. The adapter
owns inventory argv, execution argv, raw formats, canonical coverage merge and
build. The following argv are baseline contracts to fill with the consumer's
approved reporter configuration; missing reporter output is a hard failure.

| Archetype | Identity / exact inventory | Executor / raw reports / build |
| --- | --- | --- |
| web | `vitest` canonical files from `npm exec -- vitest list --filesOnly`; independently `playwright` canonical files from `npm exec -- playwright test --list --reporter=json` | Vitest run with the approved exact-file selector, `--reporter=junit --outputFile={junit} --coverage --coverage.reporter=lcov --coverage.reportsDirectory={reportDir}`; Playwright exact-file selection with `--retries=0 --reporter=junit`, `PLAYWRIGHT_JUNIT_OUTPUT_FILE={junit}` and approved LCOV collection. JUnit + LCOV; canonical line merge; `npm run build`. |
| expo | `jest` canonical files from `npm exec -- jest --listTests --json`; separately the same Playwright inventory as web | `npm exec -- jest --runInBand --runTestsByPath {unit} --reporters=default --reporters=jest-junit --coverage --coverageReporters=lcov --coverageDirectory={reportDir}`; `JEST_JUNIT_OUTPUT_FILE={junit}`. Independent Playwright runner as above. JUnit + LCOV; canonical merge; `npm exec -- expo export`. |
| flutter | `flutter` canonical `_test.dart` files from `git ls-files -z -- test`, filtered by `_test\\.dart$` | `flutter test --machine --coverage --coverage-path={coverage} {unit}`; retain stdout as `flutter-machine`, plus LCOV. Canonical merge; approved `flutter build web` or the selected platform's exact build argv. |
| android | `gradle` leaf tasks such as `:app:testDebugUnitTest`, discovered from the actual Gradle task inventory and dependency graph | `./gradlew {unit} --no-daemon --console=plain` with selected JUnit XML and JaCoCo XML outputs. Configure the actual leaf `Test` task/report output and coverage finalizer; declare its dependencies in `leafTasks`. Reject aggregate tasks and overlapping task dependency sets. Canonical merge; approved `./gradlew :app:assembleRelease --no-daemon`. |
| nx-monorepo | `nx` leaf project-target identities such as `package-a:test`, inventory `npm exec -- nx show projects --withTarget=test --json` plus configured target suffix; inspect actual target/dependency metadata | `npm exec -- nx run {unit} --excludeTaskDependencies --skipNxCache`; each approved leaf runner emits JUnit + LCOV (or explicitly selected supported raw formats). Never infer one reporter from another executor. Reject aggregates/dependency overlap. Canonical merge; `npm exec -- nx run-many -t build` with approved explicit artifact roots. |
| library-cli | `node:test` canonical files from `git ls-files -z -- test tests`, filtered by the selected test filename convention | `node --test --experimental-test-coverage --test-reporter=junit --test-reporter-destination={junit} --test-reporter=lcov --test-reporter-destination={coverage} {unit}`. JUnit + LCOV; canonical merge; `npm run build`. |

Vitest/Playwright positional filters can match more than one file. The approved
runner binding must use an exact selector and prove its selected inventory equals
the one requested identity before execution; a broad pattern is not an exact
selector. Playwright browser coverage is not automatic: install and configure the
approved instrumented coverage reporter, or report the adapter unavailable. Do
not substitute an empty coverage file. For Gradle/Nx, the inventory command must
produce an unambiguous leaf list; unsupported inventory/report formats require an
approved converter that consumes actual tool output, never a hand-maintained
success list. SDK/JDK/browser setup belongs in reviewed `setupArgv`, with pinned
versions and no secret defaults. `ADAPTERS` in the engine names install remedies.

## Determinism and completeness

Versioned manifests bind source SHA, tree, normalized sorted unique identities,
runner/build contract digest and inventory digest. Normalize Windows separators
to `/`; reject traversal, absolute paths and duplicate identities. Generate the
inventory afresh: renamed identities replace old names, deleted tests disappear
and therefore face the approved count baseline. Default weight is exactly 1;
round-robin count balancing is deterministic. One shard and more requested shards
than units are valid; clamp the latter to units and emit no empty shard. Input
permutation cannot change the manifest, shards or digest. Fan-in requires every
planned shard exactly once and its executed identity union exactly equal to the
inventory. Report paths/digests are retained, not accepted from a summary alone.

The engine parses JUnit XML, Flutter machine JSON lines, LCOV and JaCoCo XML with
separate parsers. Truncated/contradictory summaries, duplicate cases, hidden failed
or skipped cases, malformed coverage, unknown formats and missing outputs fail.
Coverage paths are remapped only through approved roots, then merged once by
canonical file/line (maximum hit count, never summing percentages). Coverage is a
line-coverage floor in version 1; branch/function percentages are not asserted.

Keep every attempt. The generated runner disables test retries. Bounded external
infrastructure retry allows at most `maxInfraRetries` (0 by default, at most 2),
requires explicit infrastructure code/reason and retains first-attempt evidence.
A required test failure remains blocking even if a rerun passes (flaky).
Quarantine requires owner, reason and unexpired expiry, and still blocks an
authoritative release. Missing first attempts or gaps in numbering fail. Upload
compact reports and raw failure diagnostics under `always()`, even on failed jobs.

`minTests`, `minUnits` and `coverageFloor` are approved baselines. During preparation,
the engine reads the previous baseline from the tracked delivery config at `BASE_SHA`:
push uses the event's previous-main SHA; manual full requires an explicit approved
`base_sha` input. Scheduled/local validation uses the current commit's first parent.
A nonempty base must be an exact ancestor preceding HEAD. Missing history fails;
a root commit or new-branch push can prove that no prior branch baseline exists.
The plan binds `{baseSha,baseline,baselineDigest,requestedDigest}` as
`adapterConfig.baselineReference`, carried through fan-in and release verification.
A changed baseline requires
`baselineApproval: {baseSha,previous,previousDigest,approvedDigest,owner,reason}`,
matching the derived previous baseline and proposed values. The approval's `previous`
value never supplies the source of truth. First installation requires the same
approval with `bootstrap:true`, `previous:null`, and the digest of null as
`previousDigest`, bound to the proven absent config/base and approved current floor.
Record that bootstrap decision in the init proposal; it is not advance write approval.
Never lower a floor to hide a regression. Review baseline changes like code; a digest
is a binding, not an independent human authorization mechanism.

## Lifecycle and release proof

PRs run the configured affected command using the exact base SHA. Main and manual
full runs inventory, plan, execute shards, fan in, build once and attest. Nightly
runs diagnose with the same full tests/build but do not publish authoritative
release evidence. PR cancellation is enabled; full/release runs never cancel one
another. The authoritative artifact name includes source SHA and producer run ID.

The manifest is `{schemaVersion,authoritative,sha,tree,suiteManifestDigest,
shardReports,coverageDigest,buildDigest,producerRunId,expiresAt,baselineDigest,
testCount,coveragePercent}`. Each raw shard report has a digest. Build files are
regular files encoded in a canonical content-addressed bundle; the build digest
binds paths and exact bytes. The attestation signs the manifest, transitively
binding all test, coverage and build evidence. GitHub's signature verification is
separate from the local digest checks.

Release resolves a tag/manual reference to an exact commit and tree, enumerates
successful full producers, downloads evidence and requires exactly one unexpired
same-SHA authoritative producer. It verifies the signed manifest against the
repository, signer workflow and source digest, then recomputes every local link.
Missing/expired/ambiguous evidence, changed tags, report/inventory/coverage/build
or producer drift is red. The verification handoff retains SHA, tree, suite digest and complete build-record
digest. Protected promotion re-verifies expiry/tag/tree and
uploads only the already-verified bundle; no build or consumer command runs there.
The fixed AWS adapter obtains an OIDC token, assumes the approved role, uploads
with a SHA-256 checksum, and checks the versioned provider readback checksum and
size. Missing credentials, unsupported provider, skipped upload or mismatched
readback is red.

All actions use immutable full commit pins with version comments. Workflow-level
permissions are empty; test/build jobs get contents-read only. The isolated
non-PR, non-nightly CI signing job alone gets attestations-write and OIDC for
